title: Pin & Variant Routing: First-Run Walkthrough Visuals and Copy
creator: Lena Morales
description: Create a set of first-run onboarding visuals, docs screenshots, and microcopy for the new Pin & Variant Routing experiences. Deliverables include annotated Figma frames for the canary/A-B/fallback flows, a short microcopy cheat-sheet for engineers, exported PNG screenshots for docs, and a small responsive kit (desktop/tablet/mobile). Focus on clarity for product-first users (PLG funnel), reduce cognitive overhead when choosing pin vs. fallback, and surface safe defaults for non-expert users.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with complete first-run walkthrough for: pin to specific model version, canary rollout, A/B split, and automatic fallback policy (all states: default, in-progress, degraded, success).
Microcopy document (one-pager) with labels, tooltip text, confirmation copy, and failure copy for SLO fallback.
3 responsive screenshot sets (desktop: 1440, tablet: 768, mobile: 375) exported as optimized PNGs + SVG assets for icons.
Annotated redlines and tokenized color/spacing tokens added to a handoff page in Figma.
Engineering handoff PR opened with exported assets, copy, and a short implementation checklist.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with PM (Marcus Lee) and Eng lead (Samira Khan). Agreed scope: first-run only, not deep settings page.
2026-03-04: Low-fidelity sketches for 6 key screens completed (decision matrix + preview + confirmation).
2026-03-07: High-fidelity Figma frames created for desktop main flow (canary + pin). Added initial microcopy draft.
2026-03-10: Added A/B split variants and fallback degraded state visuals; imported tokenized colors and spacing.
2026-03-12: Internal design critique with Product; incorporated simplification feedback (reduce toggles, clearer call-to-action).
2026-03-13: Generated doc screenshots and exported PNGs for docs team; started accessibility contrast pass.
2026-03-14: Design ready for review — posted Figma link and PRD note for engineering review.
feedback: Marcus Lee (PM): Please simplify the initial choice modal; most users should pick 'pin latest stable' by default. Can we add a brief 'Why pin?' tooltip?
Samira Khan (Eng): Add a 4th state that represents 'fallback to regional capacity' to cover on-call routing behavior; also request SVG icon set.
Accessibility review (quick pass): Ensure CTA contrast >= 4.5:1 and that status badges include text labels (not just color).
Design lead (Anya Petrov): Consider collapsing model selection when integrated with Optimize suggestions to reduce cognitive load.
risks_and_assumptions: Assume backend supports tagging requests with rollout variant id for analytics; if not, we'll surface reduced telemetry in UI.
Risk: overriding defaults for advanced users could confuse PLG funnel; need clear progressive disclosure.
Assume Optimize integration will provide recommended pin target; design should hide manual selection if recommendation present.
next_steps: Address PM and Eng feedback: add 'why pin?' tooltip copy and a regional fallback visual (due 2026-03-16).
Finalize accessibility pass and update color tokens (due 2026-03-17).
Prepare engineering handoff PR with exported assets and an implementation checklist (create PR by 2026-03-18).
Coordinate with Docs to stage screenshots in the quickstart landing page and notify Growth for PLG onboarding tests.
notes_for_engineering: Provide these exports: 1x PNG @2x for each breakpoint, 1x SVG for each icon, and JSON file with token names for spacing/colors.
Microcopy strings are in the microcopy doc in Figma comment layer — please treat them as source-of-truth until final sign-off.

Confirm status badges include both icon and readable text for color-blind accessibility.
